knowledge_point.title: Finding a Point on a Line That Is Closest to a Given Point

question.:question/problem:
![](closest-c4144935cf51fe18e99213bf.png)

Find the point on the line $2y+3x=9$ that is closest to the point $(-8,10)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The closest point is where the given line meets the perpendicular line through $(-8,10)$.

First, rewrite the given line in slope-intercept form:

$$
\begin{aligned}2y+3x&=9 \\ 2y&=-3x+9 \\ y&=-\frac{3}{2}x+\frac{9}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

The given line has slope $-\frac{3}{2}$, so the perpendicular slope is $\frac{2}{3}$, its negative reciprocal. Using point-slope form,

$$
\begin{aligned}y-y_1&=m(x-x_1) \\ y-(10)&=\frac{2}{3}\left(x-(-8)\right) \\ y&=\frac{2}{3}x+\frac{16}{3}+(10) \\ y&=\frac{2}{3}x+\frac{46}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

We now solve the system

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}y &=-\frac{3}{2}x+\frac{9}{2} \\ y &=\frac{2}{3}x+\frac{46}{3}\end{aligned}\right.
$$

by setting the expressions for $y$ equal and collecting terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{2}x+\frac{9}{2}&=\frac{2}{3}x+\frac{46}{3} \\ \left(-\frac{3}{2}-\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)\right)x&=\frac{46}{3}-\left(\frac{9}{2}\right) \\ -\frac{13}{6}x&=\frac{65}{6} \\ x&=-5\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute into the given line:

$$
\begin{aligned}y&=-\frac{3}{2}\left(-5\right)+\left(\frac{9}{2}\right) \\ y&=\frac{15}{2}+\left(\frac{9}{2}\right) \\ y&=12\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the point on the line $2y+3x=9$ closest to $(-8,10)$ is $(-5,12)$.

knowledge_point.title: Finding a Point on a Line That Is Closest to a Given Point

question.:question/problem:
![](closest-537c5f20df1f93a2b7d4e46d.png)

Find the point on the line $2y-3x=6$ that is closest to the point $(5,4)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The closest point is where the given line meets the perpendicular line through $(5,4)$.

First, rewrite the given line in slope-intercept form:

$$
\begin{aligned}2y-3x&=6 \\ 2y&=3x+6 \\ y&=\frac{3}{2}x+3\end{aligned}
$$

The given line has slope $\frac{3}{2}$, so the perpendicular slope is $-\frac{2}{3}$, its negative reciprocal. Using point-slope form,

$$
\begin{aligned}y-y_1&=m(x-x_1) \\ y-(4)&=-\frac{2}{3}\left(x-(5)\right) \\ y&=-\frac{2}{3}x+\frac{10}{3}+(4) \\ y&=-\frac{2}{3}x+\frac{22}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

We now solve the system

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}y &=\frac{3}{2}x+3 \\ y &=-\frac{2}{3}x+\frac{22}{3}\end{aligned}\right.
$$

by setting the expressions for $y$ equal and collecting terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{2}x+3&=-\frac{2}{3}x+\frac{22}{3} \\ \left(\frac{3}{2}-\left(-\frac{2}{3}\right)\right)x&=\frac{22}{3}-(3) \\ \frac{13}{6}x&=\frac{13}{3} \\ x&=2\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute into the given line:

$$
\begin{aligned}y&=\frac{3}{2}\left(2\right)+(3) \\ y&=3+(3) \\ y&=6\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the point on the line $2y-3x=6$ closest to $(5,4)$ is $(2,6)$.

knowledge_point.title: Finding a Point on a Line That Is Closest to a Given Point

question.:question/problem:
![](closest-22a07c19eb951082f7065985.png)

Find the point on the line $3y-2x=-1$ that is closest to the point $(-6,0)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The closest point is where the given line meets the perpendicular line through $(-6,0)$.

First, rewrite the given line in slope-intercept form:

$$
\begin{aligned}3y-2x&=-1 \\ 3y&=2x-1 \\ y&=\frac{2}{3}x-\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

The given line has slope $\frac{2}{3}$, so the perpendicular slope is $-\frac{3}{2}$, its negative reciprocal. Using point-slope form,

$$
\begin{aligned}y-y_1&=m(x-x_1) \\ y-(0)&=-\frac{3}{2}\left(x-(-6)\right) \\ y&=-\frac{3}{2}x-9+(0) \\ y&=-\frac{3}{2}x-9\end{aligned}
$$

We now solve the system

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}y &=\frac{2}{3}x-\frac{1}{3} \\ y &=-\frac{3}{2}x-9\end{aligned}\right.
$$

by setting the expressions for $y$ equal and collecting terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3}x-\frac{1}{3}&=-\frac{3}{2}x-9 \\ \left(\frac{2}{3}-\left(-\frac{3}{2}\right)\right)x&=-9-\left(-\frac{1}{3}\right) \\ \frac{13}{6}x&=-\frac{26}{3} \\ x&=-4\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute into the given line:

$$
\begin{aligned}y&=\frac{2}{3}\left(-4\right)+\left(-\frac{1}{3}\right) \\ y&=-\frac{8}{3}+\left(-\frac{1}{3}\right) \\ y&=-3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the point on the line $3y-2x=-1$ closest to $(-6,0)$ is $(-4,-3)$.
